These arise in a broad spectrum of problems ranging from biology and particle physics to social networks and recommendation systems. Despite the plethora of different models for deep learning on graphs, few approaches have been proposed for dealing with graphs that are dynamic in nature (e.g. evolving features or connectivity over time). We present Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs), a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events. Thanks to a novel combination of memory modules and graph-based operators, TGNs significantly outperform previous approaches while being more computationally efficient. (4) For interaction events involving two nodes i i and j j , the memories of both nodes are updated after the event has happened. For node-wise events, only the memory of the related node is updated. Here, mem \mathrm{mem} is a learnable memory update function, e.g. a recurrent neural network such as LSTM ( Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997 ) or GRU ( Cho et al., 2014 ) . Embedding. The embedding module is used to generate the temporal embedding 𝐳 i ​ ( t ) \mathbf{z}_{i}(t) of node i i at any time t t . The main goal of the embedding module is to avoid the so-called memory staleness problem ( Kazemi et al., 2020 ) . Since the memory of a node i i is updated only when the node is involved in an event, it might happen that, in the absence of events for a long time (e.g. a social network user who stops using the platform for some time before becoming active again), i i ’s memory becomes stale. While multiple implementations of the embedding module are possible, we use the form: 𝐳 i ​ ( t ) = emb ⁡ ( i , t ) = ∑ j ∈ 𝒩 i k ​ ( [ 0 , t ] ) h ⁡ ( 𝐬 i ​ ( t ) , 𝐬 j ​ ( t ) , 𝐞 i ​ j , 𝐯 i ​ ( t ) , 𝐯 j ​ ( t ) ) , \mathbf{z}_{i}(t)=\mathrm{emb}(i,t)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal{N}^{k}_{i}([0,t])}h\left(\mathbf{s}_{i}(t),\mathbf{s}_{j}(t),\mathbf{e}_{ij},\mathbf{v}_{i}(t),\mathbf{v}_{j}(t)\right), where h h is a learnable function. This includes many different formulations as particular cases: Identity (id): emb ⁡ ( i , t ) = 𝐬 i ​ ( t ) \mathrm{emb}(i,t)=\mathbf{s}_{i}(t) , which uses the memory directly as the node embedding. Time projection (time): emb ⁡ ( i , t ) = ( 1 + Δ ​ t ​ 𝐰 ) ∘ 𝐬 i ​ ( t ) \mathrm{emb}(i,t)=(1+\Delta t\,\mathbf{w})\circ\mathbf{s}_{i}(t) , where 𝐰 \mathbf{w} are learnable parameters, Δ ​ t \Delta t is the time since the last interaction, and ∘ \circ denotes element-wise vector product.
